answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down on the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused cards without looking.

answers.answer: Both setups start with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in the player's garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water. The score marker starts at 1 in a four-player game and 0 in a three-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, Swordmaster beside board, three troops garrisoned, nine in supply, 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing you skip the rest of Player Turns and cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. On Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns optional; once Revealed, turns are skipped. Reveal: resolve just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: A Plot Intrigue may be played before placing your Agent, and resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card used to send that Agent or from the destination resolve after placement and cannot pay that same cost. One card can send only one Agent, using only one matching Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may be revealed instead.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot can be played first, and its pre-placement grants can pay entry; later gains cannot. Agent Turn: choose one icon; no-icon cards only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during this turn may deploy, plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for at most five deployed from those sources. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not allowed. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison, only at a Combat space; cube recruits a troop from supply into garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; the Spy stays there. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at that destination, but not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent and before receiving space or card effects to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both, though two different Spies can be used for the two effects. A Spy cannot be recalled for both effects on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence recall connected Spies; Gather is chosen just after placement before effects.

answers.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2 + 1 sandworm × 3 + 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; at least one Conflict unit is required. Combat Intrigue: eligible players have at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not bar you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and all Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: a player need not pass just because they passed earlier; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply, resets markers, and returns sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in four-player play, each tied player gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. With two tied for first in a three-player game, each gets the second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: first-place tie gives second reward; in four players exactly two tied first leave other players competing for third; no tied-first winner/card. Zero strength gets no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards once; additional worms do not multiply it further. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay 3 spice a second time to take that reward again, for 2 VP total at 6 spice; paying only once yields one instance.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double rewards; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward costs may be paid a second time.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict, take its card face up into your supply, then check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP; it is not optional. At Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, and the pair is flipped for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Combat winner procedure and Battle Icons: take card, then mandatory match check; eligible face-up cards and Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, and regain it on returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning; the first to 4 also takes the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which is lost if the token leaves. Merely tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not take the token; you must rise above them. The FAQ separately says that if the holder loses Influence after a tie, the formerly tied player takes it (or, if several were tied, the former holder chooses). If the holder falls to 3 or lower and no one has 4+, it returns to the board.
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence: separate 2- and 4-Influence rewards and Alliance transfer rules; FAQ Alliance loss clarification.

answers.answer: During Reveal, spend Persuasion to acquire Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is at the card's top right. You may pool Persuasion sources to buy one card or split a source across purchases, and acquire cards before, between, or after Reveal effects. The Row refills to five immediately, so you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile; unused Persuasion is lost.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal purchases, top-right cost, pooling/splitting, Row replacement, discard destination, and unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: At Makers, each Agent-free Maker space gains one spice in its bonus spot, adding to any already there; visiting a Maker space collects all accumulated bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Hooks are not spent when summoning. A sandworm cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; after its removal it may be summoned to any Conflict, but never placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Deep Desert/Hagga Basin space guide; Sandworms: Hooks requirement/retention and Shield Wall restrictions.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, reaching 10 or more VP or emptying the Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. The listed resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: game end, Endgame Intrigues, winner and tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with 20 standard contracts shuffled face down; two are exposed as face-up offers and the remaining 18 stay face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left out of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and Components: two offers from 20; four added cards in each deck; contrasting-back contracts only for Rise of Ix.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and available contracts, take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank contract flipped face up. If players have taken all contracts, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract requires visiting a Maker space and gaining its stated spice total that turn, including other sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts; shared contract-icon rule.

answers.answer: No. You must have held a board-space contract when you sent the Agent there, so one taken after visiting must wait until a future visit. When completed, announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: must hold it when sending Agent; on completion announce, gain rewards, flip face down, keep in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to the humans. First Player is whichever human's Objective shows the marker, and First Player alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore placement, then immediately reveal another card. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle rule.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after omitting those marked for a different player count, then deal one eligible Objective face up to each player; its First Player marker selects the first player. Shaddam Corrino IV may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit player-count mismatches, shuffle, deal face up; Shaddam not used unless playing CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if they run out. By contrast, you cannot recruit more troops if your personal supply is empty until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments are returned to it; the summary does not say to take resources from another player's supply.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources and sandworms are not meant to be limited; gains from bank and payments return to bank. Recruiting: empty troop supply prevents recruiting.

answers.answer: The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top of the deck, resolve a controlled-location defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with three or four humans pass First Player clockwise, and in a two-player game return Rival Agents to supply and pass First Player to the other human; then start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Round Start; Recall preparation for next round.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space effects, Agent-box effects and the Faction advance may be resolved in any order. No: the space entry cost and requirements must be paid/met before resolving any space or card effects, including that visit's Influence.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs/requirements before effects; space and Agent box effects in any order; Faction advance also among effects.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost and its effect can be used only once per turn, even if you can pay again; the exception is a Conflict-card reward doubled by sandworms. Most card and space effects are mandatory, but “may” effects, optional arrow costs and the black-X trash icon can be declined; direct instructions to trash a card itself are mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs and FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: A Spy icon places a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, the Spy must be placed at a post connected to a space with that icon; otherwise placement is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: empty post, recall for no effect if needed, and specified connected Agent icon restriction.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player's Agent, not your own. You cannot recall a Spy to use these effects without playing a card for an Agent turn; recalling does not waive costs or requirements. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement, though one may Infiltrate and a different one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts and FAQ—Spies: Infiltrate only another player; recall requires Agent card; one Gather per placement.

answers.answer: The controller gets the location's separate visit bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the matching Conflict places your Control marker there, replacing the opponent's. When the Conflict is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop directly from your supply to the Conflict without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Board Space Guide notes visitor and controller bonuses are separate; defensive bonus from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict, a tie for second gives each tied player the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. A tie for third gives the tied players nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody wins or takes the card, and there are no other rewards in either three- or four-player play.
answers.evidence: Combat ties and three-tied-first clarification/table.

answers.answer: In an ordinary three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second receive their rewards and third receives nothing. That remains true in a two-human game with its Rival as the third competitor; a Rival is included in the player count for these rules.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: with two or three players ordinary first and second are paid, third gets nothing; includes Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues are playable during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and only with at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game's end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down and separate from your deck; after resolving one, place it face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck empties, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards and FAQ—Intrigue deck exhaustion.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifically says so; it discards a card of your choice from your hand. Secrets' Steal Intrigue effect takes one card selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards—Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play; return ordinary cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP is retained if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ—Victory: Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once when the card is acquired, not when later played. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; deck reshuffle rule.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond works if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order. They cease to be in play when Clean Up moves them to discard.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent; the returned Agent can be used again on a later Agent turn that same round. A retreated troop goes from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ—Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A single free-choice effect granting two Influence must assign both to one Faction, not split them. A Faction-specific minimum requires the stated minimum with that Faction; an Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance/minimum requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with multiple opponents, the former holder chooses which of the formerly tied opponents receives the Alliance token. The holder loses 1 VP and the new holder gains 1 VP. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its Alliance VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence and FAQ—Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the normal five-card draw. A Plot Intrigue with an effect that applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it can be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: winning Intrigues cannot be played after tied first; reward Intrigue can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with that one Agent placement. A board-space contract is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must hold it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the two Sardaukar contracts. They are set aside before the initial contract shuffle, and only Shaddam may acquire them; when he acquires a contract, he may choose one instead of a generally available contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts only for that turn, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup, Reserved Sardaukar contracts, and FAQ—Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of the Training track; at the rightmost space it remains there for the rest of the game. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications.

answers.answer: Yes: Margot and Irulan reach 2 even when moving from 1 past 2 to 3, and can reach 2 again later by losing Influence and then moving up through 2. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM or when no contracts remain, gain 2 Solari; otherwise take a face-up contract and replace it. It is not a Faction space and gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, costs nothing, gives 1 Emperor Influence (counted once), and resolves the same contract icon. Thus only Dutiful Service automatically advances a Faction track.
answers.evidence: Faction status of contract spaces; shared contract icon rule; board-space table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Both also give all bonus spice accumulated there, even if choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Maker Hooks are not spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. One option takes Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. The other gains 1 water and optionally removes the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari on every visit, and is not a Combat space. On the first visit, place a Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On later visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains one and 6 after anyone has one. Each player may take it only once per game; the third Agent is available the same round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. The space does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Privilege; Agent-turn Faction advance applies only on a Faction space.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the free-choice Influence need not be with the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad access and not a Combat space: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and if paying 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City access and a Combat space: pay 0 for 2 Solari or 1 spice for 4 Solari; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, cost 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, cost 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, cost 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing, is not Combat, draws an Intrigue and gives 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is not Combat, gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws a card and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, costs nothing, is not Combat, and gives 1 Guild Influence plus 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ—False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire a card removed with Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat markers start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and keep the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck. The Rival is a scoring competitor, and its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall; it can win by having the most VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and two-player Rival scope/endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's counted resource total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, spend that many resources and take its third Agent, usable in the current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water, one each; spend in order Solari, spice, Intrigue, water, keeping leftovers. The summary says it spends that many resources, not that it must spend a particular mix if a choice is available. The Agent is immediately available this round.
answers.evidence: Resources and Swordmaster: total, trigger, priority order, leftovers, current-round availability.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven resources does not qualify; the thresholds are resource-specific.
answers.evidence: Resources and Swordmaster: exact resource sets spent for VP.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival selects the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by its leftmost priority icon. It gains and loses Influence VP and Alliances like a human (including 2-Influence VP and Alliance VP), but gets no resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Influence selection, Rival resources and Swordmaster; Rival Agent turns numbered Influence icons.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination card, choose only the condition-matching destination; if it is occupied, reveal a new Hagal card rather than using the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping selection depends on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner selection depends on Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination card conditions and occupied destination procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space, deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to the garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met is simply omitted; it never prevents placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons, deployment at every Combat space, non-blocking conditional bonus.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, place a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy immediately recalls the Rival's other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before a Combat-space Agent placement on that same turn, those troops can deploy with the troops recruited that turn. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore the placement, then reveal another Hagal card because that card did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Agent turns Place Spy rule.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects all accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. With Maker Hooks and an unprotected Conflict, it summons one worm at Hagga Basin or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or if Shield Wall protection prevents summoning, it takes base spice instead: 2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. It does not lose the bonus spice when choosing worms.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces; Shield Wall protection.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to the Rival's strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. This happens before humans' normal Combat Intrigue window, so humans may act afterward. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival can gain control bonuses, the defensive troop from supply, battle-icon VP, and sandworm-doubled rewards normally. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal-effect resolution, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving, so it is not fixed at the first setting. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the track's beginning.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn—Resolve Reveal Effects; Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup—Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. The icon itself is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate optional recalls for their stated effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon and separate recall-without-card effects.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified; it does not trash the card.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm doubling lets you take the one-Influence reward twice, choosing the same Faction or two different Factions. This differs from a single effect that grants two Influence with free choice, which must put both Influence in one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card, not its Scheme. The Hagal Signet Ring effect triggers it directly; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is involved.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme are separate abilities.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon takes a token if the Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no additional token. Shield Wall removal works only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks it is ignored and the Wall stays; if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; each opponent with four or more Intrigues must also give you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Secrets; Intrigue card steal rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gets 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller gets 1 spice, including when the visitor and controller are the same player.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Basin and controller bonus rule.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards left from earlier rounds; those unclaimed cards remain there. Resolve the defensive bonus, then each player draws five cards, so the Conflict is revealed before the hand draw.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal Conflict on top of remaining cards, then draw five.

answers.answer: Each human puts one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of those tracks; no human starts holding one. The Shield Wall token is placed on the board below Spice Refinery during setup.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; normal setup assigns no Maker Hooks, but Alliance tokens are on track spaces.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn; play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. A player who Reveals skips the rest of Player Turns, and in normal three- or four-player play the phase ends when all players have Revealed. During Combat Intrigue, priority begins with First Player and proceeds clockwise; each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass, and a prior pass does not prevent acting later. Combat resolves after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat—Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, and Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order; they need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three listed steps; effects may resolve in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply to the Leader's left. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards, then separately shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks face down; deal five Imperium cards face up into the Row. Place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human's Combat marker starts at 0; the three Spies, Councilor and Control markers are among components in the player's supply. The four Influence cubes start on the bottom spaces of their tracks.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; initial card states; starting deck.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, Persuasion ordinarily buys any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow from the Reserve. Each card's cost is shown at the top right. These ordinary purchases are made on Reveal turns; Persuasion can be used before, between, or after Reveal effects.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards; Reveal turn—Persuasion timing.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal choice exists; declining a recall that is a cost also declines its associated benefit. Shield Wall removal is optional. Once removed, the Wall is returned to the box and cannot return later.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: placement/recall optional; Shield Wall: may remove, gone for rest of game.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon, unless the card has the Spy Agent icon and your Spy is at a connected post. Having a Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it can send an Agent to a connected space such as Shipping without recalling the Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spies: Spy Agent icon grants connected-space access; connected Spy alone does not give every card Spy access.

answers.answer: Yes. You may first play a legal Plot Intrigue on your Agent turn; resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources from the card used for the Agent and effects from the destination occur after placement, so they cannot pay the entry cost for that same visit.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot Intrigue timing and entry-cost resources.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply; proceed to Combat only after the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: two-player phase continuation and Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When the Conflict for a location you already control is revealed at Round Start, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict; it does not require visiting the location with an Agent. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive bonus; Combat cleanup resets markers.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you, then send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching board space. Resolve the Agent box of that card, not its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile, or move an Agent already on the board as the turn's placement; you place an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Clean Up; card anatomy.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, so he cannot postpone it by resolving board effects first. It governs deployment for the entire turn, including the Signet Ring recruited troop.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam; CHOAM Shaddam Signet benefits.

answers.answer: In four-player play with four different positive strengths, first, second and third place receive their printed rewards; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up into their supply, then checks it for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player ranks; winner's ordered card procedure.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed; it does not let you choose a card directly from the discard pile. The separate Intrigue draw icon draws from the Intrigue Deck.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival; retain the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token acquired later moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: all Maker Hooks in common bank; acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, update the Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window; the Reveal-turn value is not fixed. Use the adjusted strength shown on the track to resolve Combat rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat—Combat Intrigue: adjust marker when card resolves; combat uses adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Take gained Solari, spice or water from the common bank, not another player's supply. Payments of those resources are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: whenever you gain resources take them from bank; whenever you pay return them to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up onto the marked offer spaces; the rest remain face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the bank order.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: shuffle contracts face down, flip two face up, rest face down in bank.

answers.answer: Set aside both Sardaukar contracts before the initial contract shuffle; only Shaddam may acquire them, and setting them aside does not give them to him. Shuffle the remaining 18, expose two as the public offers, and leave 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and Reserved Sardaukar contracts.
